name: VPD Cadet Program
org: Vancouver Police Department, funded by the Vancouver Police Foundation
what_you_do: A free 28-week program for teen leaders. You learn teamwork, public speaking and fitness. You help the community, march in parades and go camping. You also see how police teams like the dog and boat units work.
who_can_apply: Teens going into Grade 10, 11 or 12 who live or go to school in Vancouver. Ages 14 to 17 when you apply. You must want to finish school and not miss a lot of it. You cannot have serious arrests, a record of trouble with police, or gang ties.
pay_detail: Free. The Vancouver Police Foundation pays for all program materials and fees.
deadline_text: Applications are closed for the 2026/2027 school year. The VPD page says to check back in the spring. Last pattern: the call for the class starting September 2025 was posted April 25, 2025. The last deadline was May 13, 2026.
how_to_apply: When it reopens in spring 2027, get the application package from the VPD Cadet page. Last time you emailed it to ApplyVPDCadets@vpd.ca or dropped it at a VPD station, with a report card and photo. Questions: cadets@vpd.ca.
notes: About 90 cadets a year. It is a leadership program, not police recruiting. The VPD Indigenous Cadet Program is a different summer job for ages 19 to 29. Unpaid, so BC child employment rules for paid work do not apply here. You need a Facebook account, and VPD checks your social media. Applicants get a criminal record check.
